what_the_files_show: 18 of 48 issues are proposed High after an independent calibration: FMW-001, FMW-004, FMW-008, FMW-009, TEC-002, TEC-004, TEC-011, TEC-012, TEC-013, TEC-015, TEC-022, TEC-023, TEC-024, TEC-025, TEC-026, TEC-028, TEC-029, TEC-036. Five meet every part of the test most clearly: RI-FMW-001, RI-TEC-011, RI-TEC-022, RI-TEC-028 and RI-TEC-036. Priority rests on EU benchmarks, Reform Agenda payment conditions and repeated key recommendations, not on how much evidence exists.
agent_recommendation: Validate the list, subject to G6-D02 and G6-D03.
what_changes: This list decides what the outputs lead with and which issues get policy options.

decision_needed: Should data protection law (RI-TEC-017) be High?
what_the_files_show: Calibration lowered RI-TEC-017 and RI-TEC-018 to Medium, because no report names them in a key recommendation, benchmark or payment condition. But full alignment is core acquis, is repeated in 2023 to 2025, and the 2024 and 2025 main findings record no progress. The test that excluded it was written for this stage and is stricter than the judgement rules, which ask only to consider these factors.
agent_recommendation: Override RI-TEC-017 to High. Leave RI-TEC-018 at Medium.
what_changes: High puts data protection law among the lead issues. Medium would leave a core acquis gap outside the lead group because of where the Commission happens to say it.

decision_needed: Does the key recommendation "in all sectors" cover quotas and public posts?
what_the_files_show: Non-discrimination is a key recommendation from 2020 to 2025. RI-FMW-002 (permits and quotas) and RI-FMW-003 (public posts) are proposed Medium because they are not named in it. From 2023 to 2025 it says "in all sectors", which could include them.
agent_recommendation: Keep both at Medium: the wording does not name them, and RI-FMW-001 already leads for Chapter 2.
what_changes: High would give Chapter 2 three more lead issues and change where options focus.

decision_needed: Which issues go to the comparator pilot (run 1b)?
what_the_files_show: The procedure asks for two or three issues with importance for accession, a clear unresolved gap, and likely comparator evidence. Comparator availability below is an expectation, not yet checked.
agent_recommendation: RI-FMW-001 (nationality discrimination in access to employment: open and persistent, recently acceding states had to remove the same conditions); RI-TEC-028 (interoperability platform underused: persistent, and a problem of use rather than law); RI-TEC-036 (national e-services portal: persistent, with regional peers running similar portals).
what_changes: This fixes run 1b. It gives one Chapter 2 and two technology issues; the two technology issues are related, so you may prefer RI-TEC-022 (cybersecurity framework) for breadth.

decision_needed: Does legal alignment reviewed by the Commission count as improving?
what_the_files_show: RI-TEC-011, RI-TEC-022 and RI-TEC-025 are proposed improving because laws were adopted and the Commission reviewed them, unlike RI-TEC-002 and RI-TEC-004, lowered to persistent because they rested on adoption alone. Applying the laws is still open: the eID amendments apply only from June 2027, and the Commission rated a communications law step not achieved.
agent_recommendation: Keep improving for these three, with the gap as partly addressed, and say in the outputs that the improvement is legal only.
what_changes: Persistent would mean no technology issue with a major EU law shows progress, which is a much bleaker headline. Adoption is never success, so the wording matters.

decision_needed: Split any more issues before the outputs?
what_the_files_show: Three issues combine parts moving in different directions: RI-TEC-012 (regulator independence and market oversight), RI-TEC-022 (framework and coordination) and RI-TEC-007 (contact point and register). RI-TEC-036 still holds 466 items after the split at G5.
agent_recommendation: Do not split now: splitting would mean a new taxonomy version and repeating judgements. Name the different parts in the dossier and outputs.
what_changes: Splitting would give sharper findings at the cost of another round. It could change direction and tractability for those issues.

decision_needed: Validate the other tier 3 judgements in bulk?
what_the_files_show: All tier 3 rows are on the Tier 3 sheet: direction, gap and tractability for 48 issues, and success and attribution for 42 links. An independent check changed few. 19 links are rated worked, mostly on Commission statements without measured results, 7 of them on roaming, and the dossiers say so.
agent_recommendation: Validate in bulk, apart from any override you make in the issue dossiers.
what_changes: Validated judgements are never overwritten later: they are flagged for re-review instead.

decision_needed: Confirm the State Audit Office as independent, though filed under government?
what_the_files_show: It was rated independent at G2 (SQ-00137, SQ-00138), so its findings count as evidence of success or failure, unlike government reporting. Four links rated failed rest mainly on it.
what_changes: If not, those links fall to insufficient evidence.

decision_needed: Note the unresolved reading of Art. 122 of the data protection law.
what_the_files_show: In the unofficial translation, Art. 122 reads as suspending core chapters of the law until accession, which seems unlikely. No judgement relies on it. Only the official text can settle it, and it is not in the source set.
agent_recommendation: Note it as open, and do not rely on it. Check the official text only if the point is used.
what_changes: Could matter for RI-TEC-017 if the wording proved accurate.
